question: Should Gateway public-network hardening be accepted with always-on request throttling, auto-HSTS, auth audit logging, and fail-closed bind fallback changes, or should those behaviors be narrowed behind explicit opt-in/config before merge?
rationale: This PR changes exposed Gateway security boundaries, config/default behavior, runtime logging, and fallback behavior; repository policy treats those as compatibility and upgrade-sensitive choices that automation cannot approve.

options.title: Narrow before merge
options.body: Require schema/help/docs, focused tests, explicit opt-in or maintainer-approved defaults, a clean rebase, and real behavior proof before reconsidering the branch.

options.title: Approve new defaults
options.body: Maintainers may explicitly accept always-on throttling, auto-HSTS, audit logging, and fail-closed bind behavior, but the branch still needs upgrade proof and the current review blockers fixed.

options.title: Close and restart smaller
options.body: Close this conflicted branch and ask for a smaller maintainer-sponsored PR around one hardened Gateway surface at a time.

recommendation.title: Narrow before merge
recommendation.body: Require schema/help/docs, focused tests, explicit opt-in or maintainer-approved defaults, a clean rebase, and real behavior proof before reconsidering the branch.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest available person-level signal from Gateway auth-rate-limit, client-IP, HSTS, and security review history.
